andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh orders urgent crop-protection measures amid severe rainfall deficit
facts: At a review meeting on 13 September, Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu directed officials to provide protective irrigation and use available water sources to reduce crop losses.
From 1 June to 12 September, the State received 218.2 mm of rainfall against a normal 476.1 mm—a 54.2% deficit.
Kharif crops had been sown over 26.50 lakh hectares, about 74% of the normal area.
Crop stress was reported in 284 mandals and 1,792 Rythu Seva Kendras/villages, affecting 2,44,443 hectares.
Kurnool, Nandyal and Anantapur were among the most affected districts; red gram and cotton were reported as the worst-affected crops.
Officials were asked to update crop-health data, complete surveys, promote less water-intensive crops and coordinate irrigation resources.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: Andhra Pradesh’s El Niño-related rainfall deficit and Kharif crop stress were already being tracked. Today: the Agriculture Minister reviewed the situation and directed urgent protective irrigation, crop-survey updates and promotion of less water-intensive crops. The State’s response remains ongoing.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Monsoon variability, rain-fed agriculture and drought mitigation in Andhra Pradesh
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: For the period 1 June–12 September 2026, the reported rainfall deficit was 54.2%; the review identified 284 mandals with crop stress.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how district-level crop monitoring, protective irrigation and crop diversification can reduce drought losses, while addressing the limits of emergency measures under prolonged rainfall deficits.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The review covered Andhra Pradesh; Kurnool, Nandyal and Anantapur were identified among the districts with the largest affected crop areas.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh steps up seasonal disease surveillance and district-level control measures
facts: On 13 September, Health Minister Y. Satya Kumar Yadav directed officials to intensify statewide measures against seasonal and infectious diseases.
The Minister called for immediate mosquito-control measures in areas reporting dengue cases and continuing surveillance for scrub typhus.
The State had recorded 941 scrub-typhus cases; officials reported rising cases in Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.
Food- and water-borne disease cases in Srikakulam were reported to have risen from 34 to 408; the statewide reported total was 930.
The Minister called for targeted checks on drinking-water sources and food hygiene in Srikakulam, and regular checks of drinking-water sources in Kurnool amid typhoid cases.
andhraPradesh.summary: The Health Minister reviewed disease trends and directed district-specific surveillance and prevention measures on 13 September. The reported concerns included scrub typhus in forest-fringe districts and food- and water-borne illness in Srikakulam; the directions were operational instructions, not a newly launched scheme.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Public health surveillance, vector-borne disease control and safe water governance
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The reported scrub-typhus total was 941; Srikakulam reported 408 food- and water-borne disease cases, according to the 13 September report.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine how routine surveillance, interdepartmental coordination, safe-water monitoring and rapid vector control can strengthen district-level public-health preparedness.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The measures applied statewide, with reported disease concerns in Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam, Srikakulam, Kurnool and Anakapalli districts.

andhraPradesh.headline: Updated rain advisory covers additional Andhra Pradesh districts as low-pressure system moves inland
facts: On 13 September, the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority forecast isolated moderate-to-heavy rain with thunderstorms in Manyam, Polavaram, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Eluru districts.
Moderate rain was also forecast in Anakapalle, East Godavari, West Godavari, NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla and Palnadu districts.
The advisory described a low-pressure area over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining areas, expected to move west-northwest across Vidarbha.
South Coastal Andhra was forecast to receive moderate rain; Rayalaseema was forecast to receive light rain at isolated places.
Residents were advised to avoid standing near trees or hoardings, and fishermen were advised not to venture into the sea.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: the 11 September advisory warned of rain associated with a low-pressure area near the north Andhra–south Odisha coast. Today: a 13 September forecast described the system over south Chhattisgarh and listed districts expecting rain and thunderstorms. This is a forecast update, not confirmation that the predicted rainfall occurred.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Bay of Bengal weather systems, monsoon rainfall and state disaster-risk communication
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The 13 September advisory was a forecast for specified districts; it should not be treated as an observed rainfall report.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how timely, district-specific forecasts and clear public advisories can reduce weather-related risks while supporting preparedness in vulnerable coastal and tribal districts.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The forecast named multiple Andhra Pradesh districts, including Manyam, Polavaram, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Eluru.

national.headline: Gujarat releases Great Indian Bustard conservation action plan; reviews cheetah and grassland programmes
facts: The Union Environment Minister released the Gujarat Action Plan for Great Indian Bustard (GIB) conservation at Bhuj, Kachchh.
The Wildlife Institute of India prepared the plan with the Gujarat Forest Department.
It targets a minimum viable population of more than 30 birds and 200–500 sq. km. of safe, contiguous habitat.
The immediate focus is the approximately 200 sq. km. Lala–Rawa landscape; about 11 sq. km. of grassland at Naliya has been restored.
The review reported 52 cheetahs in India, including 49 born in India; protected habitat across Kuno and Gandhi Sagar was reported at 3,428 sq. km.
national.summary: The Environment Ministry released a science-based Gujarat action plan for the Critically Endangered Great Indian Bustard and reviewed Project Cheetah and grassland restoration. The plan links species recovery with habitat restoration, grazing management and reduction of infrastructure-related threats.
national.staticLink: Species conservation, in-situ conservation, grassland ecosystems and landscape-level habitat management.
national.prelimsTakeaway: GIB is Critically Endangered; the Gujarat plan focuses on the Lala–Rawa landscape in Kachchh and sets a target of over 30 birds with 200–500 sq. km. of habitat.
national.mainsAngle: Assess why species-specific protection must be combined with landscape restoration, community participation and mitigation of infrastructure threats.

national.headline: Dryland Congress adopts Delhi Declaration on Drylands
facts: The three-day Dryland Congress 2026 concluded in New Delhi with adoption of the Delhi Declaration on Drylands (3D).
The declaration calls for collaboration, knowledge exchange, innovation and collective action on dryland agriculture.
Participating governments, institutions, partners and delegates endorsed the declaration at the closing plenary.
Congress recommendations highlighted stronger dryland data systems, foresight work and research-linked living laboratories.
The closing day coincided with the United Nations Day for South-South Cooperation.
national.summary: Previous: coverage focused on the UN Day for South-South Cooperation and global cooperation. Today: the Dryland Congress concluded and adopted the Delhi Declaration on Drylands, adding a concrete agriculture and research cooperation outcome.
national.staticLink: South-South cooperation, dryland agriculture, food security and climate-resilient development.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The Delhi Declaration on Drylands was adopted at the conclusion of the 2026 Dryland Congress in New Delhi.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how South-South and triangular cooperation, shared agricultural research and robust data can strengthen resilience in dryland regions.

sources.title: Dryland Congress 2026 Concludes with Delhi Declaration on Drylands

national.headline: India beat Sri Lanka to win the 2026 Women’s T20 Asia Cup
facts: India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup 2026 final at Dubai International Stadium.
India scored 183/5 in 20 overs; Sri Lanka were all out for 111 in 20 overs.
The final was played in Dubai on 13 September 2026.
India were the champions and Sri Lanka the runners-up.
national.summary: India won the Women’s T20 Asia Cup final, defeating defending champions Sri Lanka by 72 runs in Dubai. The official match result recorded India at 183/5 and Sri Lanka at 111.
national.staticLink: Regional sports competitions and the role of sporting bodies in international tournaments.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The 2026 Women’s T20 Asia Cup final was played in Dubai; India beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs.
national.mainsAngle: Use the result to discuss the growth of women’s sport, athlete development and the role of sustained institutional support.

national.headline: India announces hosting of World Circular Economy Forum 2026 in Gandhinagar
facts: India announced that it would host the World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF) 2026 in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, from 15–18 September.
The announced theme is “Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity”.
The forum is planned with more than 2,000 stakeholders from over 65 countries and 125+ exhibitors.
The listed organisers include India’s Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, the Central Pollution Control Board, the Government of Gujarat and Finland’s Sitra.
PIB describes the event as a first for South Asia.
national.summary: India announced Gandhinagar as the host city for WCEF 2026, a forum focused on circular finance, cross-sector partnerships and innovation. The announcement described the gathering as a first for South Asia; the event was scheduled for 15–18 September, so it had not yet taken place on the briefing date.
national.staticLink: Circular economy, resource efficiency, recycling and sustainable production and consumption.
national.prelimsTakeaway: WCEF 2026 was announced for Gandhinagar, Gujarat, under the theme “Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity”.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how circular-economy policy can reduce material waste while supporting innovation, finance and sustainable growth.

national.headline: CAZRI moth-bean varieties withstand a 35-day dry spell during Kharif 2026
facts: ICAR–Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI), Jodhpur, reported field resilience in four moth-bean varieties: CAZRI Moth-4, Moth-5, Moth-6 and Moth-7.
The varieties were observed during Kharif 2026 in western Rajasthan under a dry spell of about 35 days, from 3 August to 7 September.
The institute reported that the varieties maintained growth and pod development despite moisture stress.
Moth bean is an important pulse crop of hot arid regions; the PIB report estimated cultivation over nearly 10 lakh hectares nationally.
The varieties are being multiplied for seed production, with seed production reported on seven hectares at CAZRI’s research farm.
national.summary: CAZRI reported that four of its moth-bean varieties maintained growth and pod development through a prolonged moisture-stress period during Kharif 2026. The field results highlight the role of crop breeding and moisture-conserving agronomy in adapting dryland agriculture to rainfall variability.
national.staticLink: Dryland farming, pulses, crop-breeding research and climate adaptation in agriculture.
national.prelimsTakeaway: CAZRI is based in Jodhpur; its CAZRI Moth-4 to Moth-7 varieties were reported to withstand a 35-day dry spell in Kharif 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how locally adapted varieties, seed systems and agronomic practices can reduce climate risks for dryland farmers.

sources.title: CAZRI Moth Bean Varieties Demonstrate Remarkable Resilience During El Niño Year
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

national.headline: Railways reports 5.4% freight-loading growth and five new Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals in August
facts: A Ministry of Railways update published on 13 September reported 137.9 million tonnes of freight loaded in August 2026, up from 130.9 million tonnes in August 2025.
The reported year-on-year increase in freight loading was 5.4%; freight revenue was reported 6.27% higher than in August 2025.
Five Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals were commissioned during August, taking the reported total to 149 as of 31 August 2026.
The five terminals are at Shivlakha, Gujarat; Nalli, Tamil Nadu; Shaktinagar, Uttar Pradesh; Deoragram, Madhya Pradesh; and Brajrajnagar, Odisha.
Fourteen Amrit Bharat services were regularised during August, taking the reported total to 86.
national.summary: The Ministry of Railways released August 2026 operational figures, reporting higher freight loading and five additional Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals. It also reported that 14 Amrit Bharat services were regularised during the month.
national.staticLink: Rail-based logistics, multimodal transport, infrastructure development and economic connectivity.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The August 2026 railway update reported 137.9 million tonnes of freight loading and 149 commissioned Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals by month-end.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how freight terminals and rail connectivity can reduce logistics bottlenecks and support regional economic integration.

national.headline: INS Kulish arrives at Cambodia’s Ream Naval Base during Eastern Fleet deployment
facts: Indian Navy ship INS Kulish arrived at Ream Naval Base, Cambodia, on 12 September 2026.
The port call is part of the Indian Navy’s Eastern Fleet Operational Deployment.
The announced programme includes professional interactions, familiarisation visits and structured naval engagements with the Royal Cambodian Navy.
PIB linked the visit to India’s Act East Policy and MAHASAGAR vision.
The Ministry of Defence said the engagement aims to strengthen maritime cooperation and professional links between the two navies.
national.summary: INS Kulish made a port call at Cambodia’s Ream Naval Base as part of the Eastern Fleet’s operational deployment. The visit includes naval engagement and professional exchanges with Cambodia’s navy.
national.staticLink: India’s Act East Policy, maritime diplomacy and naval cooperation in the Indo-Pacific.
national.prelimsTakeaway: INS Kulish’s Ream Naval Base port call is part of the Indian Navy’s Eastern Fleet Operational Deployment.
national.mainsAngle: Explain how naval port calls and professional exchanges contribute to India’s maritime outreach and regional partnerships.

national.headline: DAHD reviews Delhi’s lumpy skin disease response and vaccination coverage
facts: The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying reviewed the lumpy skin disease situation with Delhi authorities on 13 September 2026.
The department reported about 584 active cases in Delhi as of that date and said the situation was under control, with no cattle deaths reported.
More than 45,950 animals had been vaccinated against the disease in Delhi during 2026.
The recommended measures included vaccination, active surveillance, isolation, vector control, disinfection and biosecurity.
The review stressed coordination with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi, gaushalas and other stakeholders.
national.summary: DAHD reviewed lumpy skin disease surveillance and control measures in Delhi, reporting active cases alongside vaccination efforts. The department emphasised continued vaccination, monitoring and biosecurity rather than describing the outbreak as eliminated.
national.staticLink: Animal health, zoonotic-disease surveillance, veterinary public health and One Health governance.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Lumpy skin disease is a cattle disease; the Delhi review emphasised vaccination, surveillance, isolation and vector control.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the importance of coordinated veterinary surveillance and biosecurity in managing livestock disease risks.

international.headline: India and South Africa discuss strategic partnership; India invites South Africa to consider Big Cat Alliance membership
facts: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met South African President Cyril Ramaphosa on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.
The leaders reviewed bilateral cooperation and agreed to maintain close coordination in multilateral forums.
India invited South Africa to consider joining the International Big Cat Alliance, citing cooperation linked to cheetah translocation.
The meeting reinforced the India–South Africa strategic partnership and its historical, cultural, economic and people-to-people foundations.
international.summary: The leaders reviewed bilateral ties and discussed global issues of mutual interest during the BRICS Summit. India’s invitation to South Africa to consider joining the International Big Cat Alliance was a specific new cooperation proposal.
international.staticLink: India’s foreign relations; BRICS; international cooperation for wildlife conservation.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the meeting’s venue and date, the leaders, and the International Big Cat Alliance invitation.
international.mainsAngle: Use the meeting to discuss how India can combine multilateral diplomacy with South–South cooperation and biodiversity partnerships.

international.headline: EU and FAO launch €5 million climate-resilience initiative for Afghanistan’s agrifood systems
facts: The European Union and the Food and Agriculture Organization launched a €5 million initiative in Afghanistan.
It aims to help farmers and agribusinesses access markets, improve income reliability and withstand climate and economic shocks.
The initiative targets vulnerable households, including returnees, internally displaced people and host communities; women and youth are particular focus groups.
Four one-stop service hubs are planned to connect farmers and rural entrepreneurs with advice, specialized services, businesses and markets.
international.summary: The EU and FAO launched a new programme to strengthen climate resilience and market access in Afghanistan’s agrifood sector. Its proposed service hubs will also connect farmers to climate analysis and early-warning information.
international.staticLink: Climate-resilient agriculture; food security; international development cooperation.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The partners are the EU and FAO; the announced initiative is worth €5 million and includes four planned service hubs.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how climate information, market connectivity and locally accessible services can strengthen food security and rural livelihoods in a climate-vulnerable country.

sources.title: European Union and FAO join forces to boost climate resilience of agrifood systems in Afghanistan

international.headline: IOM reports more than 85,000 people displaced in Yemen amid continued fighting
facts: The International Organization for Migration’s Displacement Tracking Matrix reported 85,818 people displaced in Yemen.
The report said 82,164 of those displacements had occurred since the beginning of September 2026.
More than 2,000 people fleeing the hostilities had reached Djibouti’s northern coast near Obock.
IOM and UN partners were supporting a response led by Djiboutian authorities, including food and water assistance at the Markazi site.
international.summary: IOM reported a sharp rise in displacement as fighting continued along Yemen’s west coast. Some people were crossing into Djibouti, where local authorities and humanitarian partners were providing assistance.
international.staticLink: Forced migration; humanitarian assistance; role of the International Organization for Migration.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The figures were reported by IOM through its Displacement Tracking Matrix; Djibouti was receiving people fleeing Yemen.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss the cross-border effects of conflict-driven displacement and the importance of coordinated humanitarian response by states and international agencies.

sources.title: IOM Yemen: Yemen Displacement Tops 85,000 as Conflict Continues, 2,000 Flee to Djibouti

international.headline: United States defeats France to win the 2026 FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup
facts: The 2026 FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup concluded in Berlin, Germany, on 13 September.
The United States defeated France 97–79 in the final.
Spain beat host Germany 81–58 in the third-place game.
The tournament ran from 4 to 13 September 2026.
international.summary: The United States won the women’s world basketball title by defeating France in the Berlin final. Spain finished third after beating Germany.
international.staticLink: International sports events; FIBA and the Basketball World Cup.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Host city: Berlin; champion: United States; runner-up: France; third place: Spain.
international.mainsAngle: International sporting events can serve as platforms for global cultural exchange and the promotion of women’s sport.

international.headline: Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Pathirage wins men’s javelin at Budapest World Athletics Ultimate Championship
facts: The men’s javelin final at the World Athletics Ultimate Championships took place in Budapest on 13 September.
Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage won with a throw of 91.09 metres.
Grenada’s Anderson Peters was second with 86.18 metres; Germany’s Julian Weber was third with 85.89 metres.
Pakistan’s Arshad Nadeem placed fifth with 81.49 metres, recorded as a season best.
international.summary: Pathirage won the men’s javelin final in Budapest with a final-round mark of 91.09 metres. Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem finished fifth, while Peters and Weber completed the podium.
international.staticLink: International athletics competitions; javelin throw; major global sporting events.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The winner was Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Pathirage; Arshad Nadeem finished fifth in the final.
international.mainsAngle: Major international competitions can strengthen regional sporting visibility and create benchmarks for athlete development.
